title: Attorney General of Florida

context.text: The August 18, 2026 primaries were canceled because each party had a single remaining candidate: incumbent Republican James Uthmeier and Democrat Jose Javier Rodriguez advanced unopposed.
Uthmeier was appointed Attorney General by Gov. Ron DeSantis after Ashley Moody was appointed to the U.S. Senate, and took office on February 17, 2025; this is his first election to the office.
Florida Phoenix's 2026 general-election voter guide and The Green Papers' candidate list show only Uthmeier and Rodriguez for the office.

candidates.name: James Uthmeier
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary; the primary was canceled with no opponent.

summary.text: James Uthmeier is the Republican Attorney General of Florida, appointed in 2025 after serving as Gov. Ron DeSantis's chief of staff and general counsel. He is seeking a first election to the office; in recent weeks his office has filed lawsuits against Meta, Pfizer and Discord and announced a statewide election-crimes operation.

background.text: Earned undergraduate and graduate degrees from the University of Florida and a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center.
Served in the U.S. Department of Commerce as senior counsel and senior advisor from 2017 to 2019.
Worked in Gov. DeSantis's office as deputy general counsel (2019), general counsel (2020) and chief of staff (October 2021 to August 2023), then managed DeSantis's 2024 presidential campaign.

priorities.text: Prosecuting child predators: his office says it has arrested more than 2,100 child predators in Florida since he took office, and it has sued the platform Discord alleging it exposed children to predators.
Holding technology and pharmaceutical companies to account through consumer-protection litigation, including actions against Meta, Pfizer and its CEO, and Discord.

Prosecuting illegal voting: his office's September 2026 release says the prosecutions come through Statewide Prosecutors working with FDLE, the Department of State and USCIS, following the state's creation of an Office of Election Crimes at the Department of State.

record.text: Announced the arrest and prosecution of 20 defendants in a statewide operation targeting illegal voting, including in the 2024 general election, alongside Gov. DeSantis.
Filed a lawsuit against Pfizer and its CEO, Dr. Albert Bourla.
Filed a motion for a temporary injunction against Meta Platforms, Inc.
Filed a lawsuit against Discord alleging the platform marketed itself to Florida families as safe for children while failing to verify ages or protect minors from strangers.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website could be loaded (teamuthmeier.com returned an error) and he has not completed the Ballotpedia survey, so priorities are drawn from his office's official releases. No direct statement on any of the guide's issue statements was found.

candidates.name: Jose Javier Rodriguez
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary; the primary was canceled with no opponent.

summary.text: Jose Javier Rodriguez is the Democratic nominee for Attorney General. A Miami attorney, he served in the Florida House (2012 to 2016) and Florida Senate (2016 to 2020), and later as a U.S. Assistant Secretary of Labor. His campaign centers on crime, costs and corruption.

background.text: Earned a B.A. from Brown University (2000) and a J.D. from Harvard Law School (2006).
Served in the Florida House of Representatives, District 112, and the Florida Senate, District 37 (2016 to 2020), where he sat on the Ethics and Elections and Judiciary committees.
Served as U.S. Assistant Secretary of Labor.

priorities.text: Protect children by holding Big Tech and social media platforms accountable, and prosecute criminal organizations and child-exploitation networks.
Investigate utilities and insurers over rates, billing and claim practices, and enforce wage-theft and environmental laws.
Root out corruption, including pursuing recovery of the $10 million at issue in the Hope Florida matter and investigating no-bid contracts.

statements.quote: Provide resources to police and prosecutors to combat violent crime and gun violence.
statements.context: From the 'Support Public Safety' item on his campaign priorities page.

record.text: Served in the Florida Senate (District 37) from November 2016 to November 2020, including as vice chair of the Judiciary Committee in 2019-2020.

candidates.researchNotes: Legislative roll-call votes were not reviewed; the record entry lists his office and committee role only.

researchNotes: Slate: the Florida Division of Elections candidate download returned no data and its candidate page was not current, so the slate rests on the Florida Phoenix voter guide and The Green Papers, which list only Uthmeier (R) and Rodriguez (D); a write-in or no-party candidate cannot be ruled out. Ballotpedia pages (blocked by an automated challenge) could not be re-read, so biographical details sourced only to Ballotpedia were not re-verified. Florida's Secretary of State is appointed, so there is no SoS race.
